name: Principal component analysis (PCA)
summary: Finds a few uncorrelated directions that capture most of the variation in many correlated variables.
inputs: Numeric matrix (rows = observations, columns = variables), usually standardised.
outputs: Components (loadings), scores per observation and explained variance.
assumptions: Features standardised when on different scales
math_summary: Finds orthogonal directions of maximal variance: eigenvectors of the covariance matrix (or right singular vectors of the centred data matrix X = U S V').
when_to_use: Extracting a few factors from many correlated series (yield-curve level, slope, curvature)
Reducing dimensionality before regression or clustering
when_not_to_use: When components must be interpretable as named drivers
pitfalls: Unstandardised inputs let one variable dominate
Look-ahead if fitted on the full sample before backtesting

compute.complexity: O(min(n p^2, n^2 p)) via SVD; randomised SVD for large data.

applicability.use_case: Yield-curve factors from government bond yields across maturities
Composite indices from many country indicators
